antonomasia: The substitution of an epithet or title in place of a proper noun.
antonym: A word which has the opposite meaning of another word.
antonymic: Of, relating to, or being an antonym or antonyms.
antonymy: The semantic relation between antonyms; the quality of being antonymous.
antral: Of or pertaining to an antrum
antrorse: Curved or pointed forward or upward.
antrum: A bodily cavity, especially one having bony walls, especially one in the sinuses.
antsier: comparative form of antsy: more antsy
antsiest: superlative form of antsy: most antsy
anuran: Any amphibian of the order Anura: any frog (narrow sense) or toad.
anuresis: The inability to urinate; the retention of urine in the bladder.
anuretic: Of, pertaining to or characterised by anuresis.
anuria: A condition in which the kidneys do not produce urine.
anuric: Of, pertaining to, causing or afflicted with anuria.
anus: The external orifice of the rectum in most mammals, teleost fish, and many invertebrates, through which feces and flatus are ejected.
anvil: A heavy iron block used in the blacksmithing trade as a surface upon which metal can be struck and shaped.
anviled: simple past and past participle of anvil
anviling: present participle and gerund of anvil
anvilled: simple past and past participle of anvil
anvilling: present participle and gerund of anvil
anxiety: An unpleasant state of mental uneasiness, nervousness, apprehension and obsession or concern about some uncertain event.
anxiously: In an anxious manner; with painful uncertainty; solicitously.
any: To even the slightest extent; at all.
anybody: Any one out of an indefinite number of persons; anyone; any person.
anyhow: In any way or manner whatever.
anything: Any object, act, state, event, or fact whatsoever; a thing of any kind; something or other.
anyways: In any way or respect, at all.
